subject: Isolated VPC deployment — data governance & optional key escrow
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Leah Meyer <leah.meyer@cedarpointhealth.com>, procurement@cedarpointhealth.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-06-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Isolated VPC deployment — initial responsibility matrix and next steps

Leah / CedarPoint team,

Thanks again for the call this morning. Attached is a first-pass responsibility matrix for the isolated VPC/on-prem-style deployment we discussed (isolated-vpc-responsibility-matrix.xlsx). The spreadsheet maps: control plane vs. tenant plane responsibilities, where customer-controlled keys live, operator access windows, and default log retention windows.

High-level notes:
- BYOK / customer-managed keys is supported. By default Redwood will not hold unencrypted tenant keys.
- We can offer an optional, customer-requested escrow for CMKs; escrow only released under a documented legal process (see proposed language in the attached).
- Operator access is narrow by default: break-glass only, recorded with multi-party approval for sensitive customer tenants.
- Cross-border telemetry replication is by-policy and can be scoped to EU-only if required.

Can you confirm the items in column G of the matrix (red lines): specifically, whether CedarPoint requires escrow to be prohibited entirely, or whether you would accept an optional escrow under strict POA/court-order conditions? If you prefer a no-escrow model we will move to a fully customer-controlled CMK path and provide a short FAQ and evidence bundle (SOC2 + KMS ops diagram).

Next step: If this looks ok, I can loop in our legal and security SMEs for a 30-minute sync. Proposed slots: Tue 6/7 10:00-10:30 PT or Wed 6/8 14:00-14:30 PT.

Attachments: isolated-vpc-responsibility-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com
+1 415-555-0182

From: Leah Meyer <leah.meyer@cedarpointhealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@cedarpointhealth.com, security@cedarpointhealth.com
Date: 2027-06-02T11:03:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Isolated VPC deployment — initial responsibility matrix and next steps

Jonas,

Thanks for the matrix — useful starting point. A few items from legal and security after an initial review (see attached CPH_DPA_redlines.docx):

1) Customer keys: CedarPoint's security policy prefers absolute customer-only key control (no escrow). If Redwood requires an escrow to meet any operational obligations, we need specific, tightly scoped escrow-release criteria (court order + independent trustee + dual-signature).

2) Operator access: break-glass must be auditable and require approval from two named CedarPoint contacts. We also want a guaranteed notification window (within 1 hour of access).

3) Logs & cross-border transfer: we plan to keep primary logs in EU region. We will not accept default replication to US unless logs are pseudonymized and encrypted with a CPH key.

4) Retention: production requestable logs should be retained 90 days; system and telemetry may be capped at 180 days but must be clearly separated.

5) Evidence: please provide SOC2 Type II summary and a diagram showing where operator break-glass flows occur and how the CMK is protected in your runtime.

We can do the legal sync as you suggested. Preferred: Tue 6/7 17:00-17:30 CET (which is Tue 10:00 PT).

Leah Meyer
Dir., Procurement & Vendor Risk
CedarPoint Health
leah.meyer@cedarpointhealth.com
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-06-03T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Isolated VPC deployment — initial responsibility matrix and next steps

Team — forwarding Leah's redlines from CedarPoint (important customer). Key asks summarized below (quoted from Leah):

- No-escrow preferred; if escrow allowed it must be court-order + trustee + dual-signature.
- Break-glass: two named CPH approvers + 1-hour notif window.
- Logs: primary EU residency, no default US replication unless pseudonymized + CPH encryption.
- Retention: requestable logs 90d; system telemetry 180d.
- Evidence: SOC2 + operator-access diagram needed.

Options for reply:
A) BYOK only (Redwood never holds unencrypted CMK). We provide step-by-step onboarding guide and evidence package. Operator break-glass flows require a customer-supplied short-lived token that we can validate.
B) Optional escrow with extremely limited release (we'd propose: sealed escrow stored with an independent escrow trustee; release requires court order + Redwood internal legal + trustee sign-off; release events logged + customer notified immediately). This is heavier but may unlock some procurement objections.

Questions for security/legal:
- Are we comfortable committing to the 1-hour notification SLA on operator break-glass? That implies faster on-call and automated notif hooks.
- Can we offer EU-only telemetry replication and a configuration flag to disable US replication at account creation? Implementation effort: likely a config + routing policy.

Suggested reply to CedarPoint: accept BYOK by default, offer the escrow as a carve-out they must opt into, and provide the SOC2 + diagram. Attach a short DPA proposal with explicit escrow-release language.

I'll draft a proposed language and send to Leah. Thoughts?

— Jonas
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Leah Meyer <leah.meyer@cedarpointhealth.com>, procurement@cedarpointhealth.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-06-04T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Isolated VPC deployment — data governance proposal and draft DPA

Leah / CedarPoint team,

Appreciate the redlines — we've reviewed with our security and legal teams. Summary of what we can commit to and proposed contract language below; I'm attaching a short DPA proposal (redwood-dpa-proposal.docx) with exact clauses.

Key commitments:
- BYOK by default: CedarPoint may supply a customer-managed CMK (BYOK). Redwood will not retain an unencrypted copy of any tenant CMK unless CedarPoint explicitly opts into escrow.
- Optional escrow: available only if CedarPoint signs the escrow addendum. Escrow storage will be with an independent trustee. Release conditions limited to a court order or mutually agreed emergency process; all releases require trustee + Redwood legal sign-off and CedarPoint notification within 1 hour of release. Proposed escrow wording is in section 4.3 of the attached DPA.
- Operator access: break-glass requires two named CedarPoint approvers (you provide the contacts). Any operator access is recorded, logged, and an automated notification is sent to the provided contacts within 1 hour.
- Logs & replication: we will allow tenant log residency to be restricted to EU region for CedarPoint accounts. If replication to other regions is requested it will be encrypted with the CedarPoint CMK and pseudonymized where applicable.
- Retention: requestable logs 90 days (default); system telemetry 180 days. We can expose configuration flags at onboarding for non-default retention windows.
- Evidence: attaching our SOC2 Type II summary and an operator-access flow diagram in the Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0B_example/cedarpoint-dpa-draft.

Next steps: I've attached the DPA draft and proposed escrow addendum. If these high-level commitments look ok, let's lock the legal sync for Tue 6/7 10:00 PT. Confirm and I'll send a calendar invite with the Redwood security lead and our counsel.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com
+1 415-555-0182

Attachments: redwood-dpa-proposal.docx (DPA draft), isolated-vpc-responsibility-matrix.xlsx (previous)
